name: Seaweed Green
lede: Seaweed Green is a dark, brownish olive, named for the color of the weed on the shore.

sections.title: A yellowish green from the tide line
sections.body:
Paterson defines seaweed green as a yellowish green [1]. His index of greens lists it among the greens, with [[sea-green]] among its neighbors [2]. The swatch here is far darker and browner than that definition suggests, so the modern swatch and the old wording do not match exactly [1][3].

The books attach no dye or pigment to the name, and give no date [1]. A close relative in sound is [[seaweed]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 3,470 hold this color at 5% of the canvas or more, as photographed, a large share of the archive, probably because dark olive browns are common in old paintings [3]. The earliest strong sample is a portrait of the artist's infant son by Christen Købke, 1845 [3]. Printed use of *seaweed green* peaked in 2013 [4]. The match counts any painting with this color covering at least a twentieth of the canvas, so it shows where the color appears in photographs of paintings, not that the painters ever called it by this name.
